answer: Co-located Beacon Triangulation** Each agent identity must continuously prove presence at a physical site by hitting a short-range radio beacon fixed to a jetty or wharf piling. Neighboring beacons along the same ridge cross-check timing, so a claimed position is confirmed by at least two independent fixed receivers. Faking thousands of identities requires thousands of real transmitters at distinct, verifiable coordinates, not just software keys. The attacker pays the cost of physical hardware, installation, and site access per identity, making mass forgery economically prohibitive.
